title: Effects of Curvature-Scalar Coupling on Vacuum Energy in Flat (3+1)-Dimensional Space-Time
authors: Volodymyr Gorkavenko, Oleh Barabash, Pavlo Nakaznyi, Mariia Tsarenkova, Nazar Yakovenko, Andrii Zaporozhchenko
abstract: We investigated how a magnetic topological defect affects the vacuum polarization of a charged massive scalar field in a flat $(3+1)$-dimensional space-time. The defect was modeled as an impenetrable to matter field finite-thickness tube with magnetic flux inside. We implemented the most general form of the Robin boundary condition on the surface of the magnetic tube, which enables a fully general analysis of the problem. We have found that in flat spacetime, the total vacuum energy generated by a magnetic topological defect depends on the curvature $ξ$, except for special cases corresponding to the Dirichlet and Neumann boundary conditions. By contrast, when Robin's general boundary conditions are imposed, the induced vacuum energy acquires an explicit dependence on the curvature coupling $ξ$, which is significant even in flat space-time. A detailed study of the dependence of the effect on the boundary condition parameter has been carried out. The obtained results highlight the nontrivial role played by boundary conditions in vacuum polarization phenomena.
summary: This paper calculates the vacuum energy induced by a magnetic topological defect on a scalar field in flat spacetime, incorporating terms dependent on spacetime curvature. The key finding is that using general boundary conditions introduces an explicit dependence on the curvature coupling constant ($\xi$), highlighting the crucial role of boundary physics in quantum vacuum effects.
main_problem: The study investigates how a magnetic topological defect influences the vacuum polarization, quantified by the induced vacuum energy, of a charged massive scalar field in flat (3+1)-dimensional spacetime.
main_result: The induced vacuum energy explicitly depends on the curvature coupling constant ($\xi$) when general Robin boundary conditions are applied, unlike special cases like Dirichlet or Neumann boundaries. This dependence is significant even in flat space-time.
method: The analysis involves solving the stationary Klein-Gordon equation using Bessel functions and calculating the renormalized expectation value of the energy-momentum tensor ($T_{00}$).
model_or_system: The system models a charged massive scalar field interacting with spacetime curvature ($\xi R$) near an impenetrable, finite-thickness cylindrical tube carrying a magnetic flux. The analysis employs the most general Robin boundary condition.
important_parameters: Curvature coupling constant ($\xi$), magnetic flux ($F$), tube radius ($r_0$), and boundary condition parameter ($	heta$).
main_assumptions: The analysis is performed in flat spacetime, and the calculation requires renormalization by subtracting the zero-flux contribution to handle divergences.
figures_summary: Figures compare dimensionless vacuum energy dependence on $	heta$ and tube thickness ($m r_0$), showing crossover points between (3+1)D and (2+1)D results.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the Lagrangian involving curvature coupling, derives the governing Klein-Gordon equation with general Robin boundary conditions, calculates the vacuum energy using $T_{00}$, and compares the resulting energy in (3+1)D to known limits and lower dimensions.
why_interesting: While focused on QFT in curved spacetime, the rigorous treatment of boundary conditions (Robin vs. Dirichlet/Neumann) and the explicit inclusion of curvature coupling ($\xi$) provide general theoretical tools applicable to effective field theories describing quantum systems near boundaries or defects.
